3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that "Kha" schedule land originally belonged to opposite party Nos.9-16 Sudhangshu Kumar and opposite party Nos.9-16 made a settlement of the above described land in favour of the plaintiff and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 on 20th Baisakh, 1358 BS. The plaintiff and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 after settlement created dwelling huts, planted fruit trees, constructed graveyard, cultivated the null land and paid rent on receipt of dakhilas and thus they had been continuing in the peaceful possession over the suit land. The settlement was made after RS operation and the State acquisition operation was not held in the locality and the record of SA Khatian was wrongly prepared as per RS khatian in the name of Shudhangshu Kumar and opposite party Nos.9-16. Thereafter the plaintiff petitioner and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 as plaintiffs filed a suit being numbered 339 of 1976 for declaration of their title over the suit land against Sudhangshu Kumar and opposite party Nos.9-16 before the court of Munsif at Jhalakati. The suit was decreed on compromise on 18-9-1976. The plaintiff petitioner and the opposite party Nos.17 and 18 on the basis of the decree dated 18-9-1976 filed Mutation Case No. 5-JK/ 1977-78 under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Jhalakati and obtained an order of mutation and accordingly a new khatian being No. 801 was opened in their names and paid Government rent and obtained dakhilas for years together. It is stated in the plaint that the opposite party No. 1 is a greedy man of the locality and the opposite party Nos. 2-8 are his associates. 

 12. On a perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the learned appellate Court below on consideration of the materials on record and documentary evidence produced by the plaintiff in TS No. 421 of 1977 has arrived at a finding that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case and proved that they are in possession of the suit land in pursuance of the auction sale of the land held earlier. It may be mentioned that the trial Court considered this evidence and observed that although they filed these papers but there is not an iota of evidence adduced by the plaintiff to show that the auction sale was acted upon and that the possession was given to the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 421 of 1977. It further appears that the appellate Court below did not take into consideration the khatian, rent receipts and exhibits filed by the plaintiff petitioner in Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 in support of their contention. Here it may be mentioned that the trial Court below on proper scrutiny and analysis of evidence adduced by the witnesses of both the parties arrive at a finding that the plaintiff petitioner, was able to prove his possession in the suit land although he has miserably failed to substantiate his contention as to the title to the suit land, but the appellate Court below did not controvert that point nor reversed the findings of the Trial Court on that point. In dismissing, Title Suit No. 421 of 1977, the trial Court discussed the evidence adduced by the witnesses of the defendant opposite party No. I of the present Rule and observed that they are highly interested and partisan witnesses and, as such, the oral testimony of the witnesses were discarded by the trial Court on that account. The appellate Court overlooked this aspect of this case and without adverting to that point only considered the documentary evidence adduced by the opposite party No. I and arrived at a finding that the opposite party No. I has been able to prove his case. It thus appears that the impugned judgment of Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 suffers from gross illegality and infirmity and that in view of the matter I am of the view that the impugned judgment so far it relates to Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 cannot be maintained.
